title: Lena and the Bakery
premise: Yara Whitlock, a single parent and owner of Marrow Bay's only bookshop, has spent ten years keeping her heart as disciplined as her ledgers. When her late grandmother's orchard deed surfaces bearing two names — hers and Elias Vane's, the estranged boy who once worked the bakery lease below the orchard and left without a word — the two are legally bound to settle the property before the bakery's lease expires. Forced into shared stewardship, Yara and Elias must untangle a decade-old betrayal involving her grandmother's will and the town council's quiet land grab, and Yara discovers the heart is less a muscle than a door she nailed shut herself. The novel ends with Yara saying the rehearsed sentence aloud — 'I choose you, and I am staying' — as they sign the deed jointly and reopen the bakery beneath the blossoming orchard.
about_author: Ada Brightwater is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who now writes love stories about stubborn people and stubborn land. She lives above a bakery she cannot resist, and insists every romance should smell faintly of yeast and rain.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. While cataloguing her grandmother's estate, Yara finds the orchard deed with two names: her own and Elias Vane's. Her daughter, Juniper, asks why her mother's hands are shaking. The beat: controlled grief cracking open into dread, as the past arrives in legalese.

chapters.title: Flour on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias returns to Marrow Bay to contest the deed, planning a two-week trip and a lawyer. Instead he finds Yara behind the bakery's boarded windows, and the town watching. The beat: guilt wearing competence as a mask; he came for property, not penance.

chapters.title: Terms of Cohabitation
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The lawyer forces a compromise: sixty days of joint stewardship before either can sell. Yara proposes rigid rules — no questions about the past. Elias agrees too quickly. The beat: two people negotiating a truce both secretly intend to break.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Clearing the orchard, Yara finds her grandmother's letters hinting the deed was deliberately split — a test, or a trap. Juniper bonds with Elias over pruning. The beat: tenderness sneaking past Yara's defenses, and the first suspicion that the betrayal wasn't Elias's alone.

chapters.title: The Council's Quiet Hand
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias discovers the town council has been buying orchard-adjacent parcels through a shell company — and that his father signed the original bakery lease under pressure the year he fled. The beat: righteous anger redirected inward, as Elias realizes he was a pawn twice over.

chapters.title: Bread at Midnight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A power outage strands them in the bakery; they bake by lantern light and Elias finally explains the night he left — a confession Yara isn't ready to receive. The beat: intimacy achieved and immediately regretted; Yara retreats behind her rehearsed sentence, unsaid.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara learns her grandmother knew about the council's scheme and used the deed to force the two of them together — and that Yara's mother helped hide the letters. The beat: the corruption theme lands at home; inheritance revealed as both gift and manipulation.

chapters.title: Sixty Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The council moves to seize the orchard via eminent domain; the town splits, and the bakery lease expires in a week. Yara and Elias pool evidence, and Yara publicly chooses the fight — and him. The beat: rising action cresting; the rehearsed sentence half-spoken, interrupted.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the council hearing, Elias exposes the shell company and Yara reads her grandmother's letters into the record. The town flips; the seizure fails. The beat: climax — public truth-telling, private terror, and the deed's purpose finally understood.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the last day of the lease, Yara says the sentence she has rehearsed for a decade: 'I choose you, and I am staying.' They sign the deed jointly and reopen the bakery as the orchard blooms. The beat: resolution — the heart, untrained at last, simply open.
